reason: I'll start with filtration so I can follow what leaves the blood and what needs to be recovered.
expectation: I expect small substances, including glucose and waste, to pass through the filter while blood cells and large proteins remain in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the route to the bladder, but I want to follow filtration first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose, salts and water through alongside waste, so the recovery tube is the next part to follow.
reaction: It was interesting that the filter doesn't just select waste.
reason: I'll follow the filtered fluid into the recovery tube to see what returns to the blood.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, while waste remains in the tube.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to finish following recovery first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to the blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to collect in the bladder.
reaction: It makes sense why filtering alone isn't enough.
reason: I'll add the ureters first because they connect the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: I expect the tubes to attach to the kidney pair, leaving the bladder to add afterward.

alternatives.reason: I could add the bladder first, but following the drainage route from the kidneys seems clearer.

effect: The ureters now connect to the kidney outlets, leaving the bladder to complete the drainage route.
reaction: The downward arrows make the route easy to follow.
reason: I'll add the bladder; it's the only available combination and completes the route from the kidneys.
expectation: I expect the ureters to lead into the bladder so it can collect urine.

effect: The ureters now connect both kidneys to the bladder, providing a continuous drainage route.
reaction: The filling comparison makes the bladder's storage role clear.
reason: I'll follow the remaining fluid into the completed drainage route; it's the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the waste-containing fluid to travel as urine through the ureters and collect in the bladder.

effect: The remaining fluid reaches the bladder as urine, completing the route while blood continues separately.
reaction: The separate arrows made the two routes clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtration and recovery was most worthwhile: it showed why useful substances have to be taken back rather than simply filtering out waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the bladder was straightforward and the only available combination, though it clearly completed the drainage route.

surprise.text: The filter lets useful glucose and water through along with waste, rather than picking out waste alone.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the recovery and drainage routes.

continue.text: I would probably continue because following the fluid from filtering to recovery and collection made the body’s plumbing understandable, although the final fittings were predictable.
